key_insight: Finite-element-guided stressor-layer patterning can turn a silicon substrate into a near-sinusoidal crystalline undulator with sub-millimeter period and nanometer-scale amplitude.
engineering_relevance: This demonstrates a fabrication path for compact crystal-based gamma sources, with geometry tuned for 5–30 GeV beams and 5–15 MeV photon output.
method: Simulated silicon substrate deformation under patterned silicon nitride stressor layers.
Optimized period, substrate thickness, and geometry to maximize sinusoidal bending and suppress higher harmonics.
Fabricated a 160 µm thick device with 10 periods and 334 µm period length based on the simulation design.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports successful fabrication and a uniform deformation extending up to 20 µm from the surface, indicating the simulated design was realized in hardware.
watch_item: Performance may be sensitive to residual higher harmonics and to fabrication tolerances in thickness, stressor patterning, and deformation uniformity.
paper_title: From Simulation to Fabrication: Realizing Silicon Crystalline Undulators with Silicon Nitride Stressor Layer Patterning
